mechanism: Forks the current World {{state}} (W) into W', executes an action in W', discards W' and returns the {{outcome}}. W remains immutable. The fork is what provides isolation, which is also its limit: only effects that flow through W are contained, so a {{sandbox}} is required wherever simulated code can reach resources the fork did not copy.
invariants: Isolation within the fork: side effects on W' do not propagate to W.
Isolation extends only to state captured by the fork. Effects reaching resources outside W require a {{sandbox}} boundary.
preconditions: W is forkable — the world state can be snapshotted at the fidelity the simulation requires
